lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: folding and hanging

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 2 — clothing care and readiness routines
objective: From a basket of clean, dry laundry, the learner separates items that should be folded (t-shirts and shorts) from items that wrinkle easily and should be hung (a button shirt or a dress), folds the flat items using a taught sleeves-in, half, half-again sequence, hangs the rest facing the same direction, and puts both groups away in their correct drawer or closet spot with a trusted adult checking the result afterward.
scenario: A basket of clean, dry laundry sits on a table near the learner's dresser and closet. The learner sorts the basket into a fold group and a hang group, folds the fold group using the taught sequence, hangs the wrinkle-prone items on hangers facing the same way, and places both groups into their storage spot while a trusted adult is nearby to check the finished result.
safetyNotes: The learner does not stand on a chair, stool, or shelf to reach a high closet rod; if a rod or shelf is out of reach, a trusted adult hangs or places that item instead.
A trusted adult stays nearby while a sliding or hinged closet door is open so it cannot swing or slide shut on the learner's fingers.
If a drawer sticks or is hard to open, the learner asks the trusted adult for help rather than forcing it.

simulationAlternative.description: If a real basket of clean laundry or a private drawer and closet are not available this week, the learner instead practices the fold sequence on two borrowed flat items, such as bath towels, and draws a labeled diagram showing exactly where a folded pile and a row of hung items would go in their storage spot.

materials: a basket of clean, dry laundry with both fold-type and hang-type items

tasks.directions: Before folding or hanging anything, look through the whole basket.

prompts.text: Count how many items in the basket should be folded and how many should be hung, and name one item you were unsure about.

tasks.directions: Fold every fold-type item using the taught sleeves-in, half, half-again sequence, then hang every wrinkle-prone item facing the same direction.

prompts.text: I laid each fold-type item flat and tucked the sleeves in before folding it in half, then in half again.
I hung every wrinkle-prone item with the buttons or zipper closed on the hanger.
I turned every hanger to face the same direction on the rod.
I did not stand on furniture to reach a high spot, and asked for help if something was out of reach.

tasks.directions: Put both the folded pile and the hung items away in their correct storage spot.

prompts.text: Describe exactly which drawer or shelf the folded items went into and which part of the closet the hung items went into.

tasks.directions: Think back over the folding and hanging you just finished.

prompts.text: Name one specific item that was tricky to fold or hang, and describe exactly what you changed to get it right.

remediation: If a learner stuffs folded items into a drawer in a loose pile instead of a stack, causing them to wrinkle again right after folding, reteach by having the learner build the stack shortest item first and press each layer flat with a hand before adding the next one.
extension: Have the learner apply the same fold sequence to a different flat item, such as a towel or pillowcase, and place it in its own storage spot.
